- **RBP-F001** (Important, rust-best-practices-agent) `crates/sc-treesitter/src/git_io.rs:243` — Correction: Yes, a helper in the shared module is the right fix, not a second local copy. Add `pub fn hash_blob(repo: &RepoRoot, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<BlobSha, JevError>` to sc_agent_types::git (feature `git`). It should reuse the private git() constructor, override stdin to piped, and map errors the way hash_bytes does now. Delete git_command and hash_bytes from git_io.rs, and update the module doc line that says the shared module has no hashing helper. If extending the shared crate is out of scope for this sprint, make the private git() constructor `pub(crate)`-adjacent or expose a documented `pub fn git_command(dir)` so there is one env policy. File a bead for the follow-up.
- **FTQ-001** (Important, flaky-test-qa) `crates/sc-treesitter/tests/support/mod.rs:20` — Correction: Make isolate_git the single scrubbing point. env_remove GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_PREFIX, GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS and GIT_CONFIG_COUNT. Also pin GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM to the null device. Use the same list as r-1's helper and as git_io::git_command so the three stay in step. This removes the leak; no retries or conditionals are needed.
- **RBQA-F001** (Important, ruthless-boundary-qa) `crates/sc-treesitter/src/git_io.rs:243` — Correction: Add a `hash_blob(repo: &RepoRoot, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<BlobSha, JevError>` helper to sc_agent_types::git (feature `git`). Until then, add a tracked exemption for git_io.rs to the ban.

Include a negative case, such as a canary fixture or a sed-injected edge, to show the gate can fail.

Better, run these runner self-tests once, in a single binary (a dedicated test target or the workspace crate that owns the file), not in every includer.
